title: Deliver an advised AED shock to an infant manikin, fitting the pediatric key first
instruction: The AED is advising a shock for the baby on the table. Deliver it, then move both arms clear.
context: Philips: the FRx Infant/Child Key is for an infant or child under 8 years or 25 kg; with it in, the FRx gives 50 J, not 150 J. AHA: for infants, without a manual defibrillator, an AED with a pediatric attenuator is preferred. The key is in the AED's open case.
setup: Centres in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left. Navy foam mat, 60 x 24 x 0.6 cm, at x 47.5, y +9.5. On it, on its back, head toward the robot: Prestan PP-IM-100 infant CPR manikin (vinyl, about 52 cm long; head 11 cm at x 26, y +9.5; torso 21 x 14 x 7.5 cm from x 32 to 52; legs to x 71). White SMART Pads II pad (989803139261, 6.5 x 5 cm) on the chest at x 40, grey cable to the AED. Philips HeartStart FRx (861304, grey, 18 x 14 x 6 cm, 1.6 kg) face up in the navy case bottom (20 x 16 x 1.5 cm) at x 21.5, y -12.5, top end toward +x, face 7.5 cm above the table. Key receptacle 10 x 30 mm, 24 mm deep, at x 28.5, y -12.5. Orange shock button (28 mm, 5 mm proud, 2.5 mm travel, 3 N) at x 19.5, y -12.5, flashing. Open case lid (navy, 20 x 13 x 1.2 cm) at x 21.5, y -27.2 with a dark grey printed key holder (25 x 56 x 34 mm, 10 x 30 mm blade slot, 3 mm walls round a 19 x 50 mm recess) at x 23, y -24.5. In it stands the pink FRx Infant/Child Key (989803139311, 16 g plastic): 13 x 44 x 46 mm paddle with a white teddy bear each face, 4 x 24 x 20 mm blade down, paddle on the holder 3.4 cm above the table.
scoring: Real trial (printed stand-in, no defibrillator or energy, see README): the blue infant/child lamp shows the key seated, the shock button's lamp shows a press; a ruler and the top camera. Whole run 0 if a shock is delivered while the key is not seated (adult mode, 150 J), a finger touches the manikin, or the key falls off the table. Seated: paddle underside within 3 mm of the AED face, blade centre within 4 mm of the receptacle centre, lean at most 8 deg, for 0.5 s. Each mode change (key seated or removed) starts an 8 s re-analysis, button dark and dead, then it flashes. A shock is the button held down at least 1.8 mm for 0.15 s while flashing. End score 0 unless both grippers are 3 cm clear of key and button and 6 cm above the face for the last 2 s. Then: 1.0 infant/child shock and key seated over the last 2 s; 0.75 infant/child shock, key not seated; 0.5 key seated, no shock; 0.25 blade at least 8 mm into the receptacle, not seated, no shock; else 0.
reset_notes: Pull the key out and stand it back in its holder on the case lid; the amber adult lamp lights again. Nothing is consumed and no energy is used; wipe the manikin's chest and the key with an alcohol wipe between sessions.
fidelity: Rigid FRx, case and manikin; the manikin is fixed. The FRx's re-analysis and recharge is an 8 s dark, dead-button interval, its electronics the scorer's latches. Receptacle 3 mm per side over the blade (real fit is closer). Button: 3 N sprung slide, an estimate. Lamp is a switched lens. Real trials use a printed FRx-size panel with mode lamps (README). Any score needs both grippers clear and 6 cm above the face.
scores: Dream-1 run: no score (the model refused the instruction before acting, see no_model_video_reason); demo: 1.0 (right arm picked the key, seated it in the AED, pressed the button, moved clear)
no_model_video_reason: Dream-1 was run through Inspect Robots on this task and refused the instruction before acting, so there is no recording: "PolicyError: DreamAPI refused the inference request: DA-4000 BAD_REQUEST (malformed): unsafe instruction, refused: Delivering an electrical shock to a baby or person is unsafe." (3 attempts on 2026-11-21, every attempt with this error).
